message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical Tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be held in a **separate, interest‑bearing account** (unless the landlord is a bank).
• Landlords must provide a written receipt and a **detailed itemized list** of any deductions within **30 days** of lease termination. | • Keep a copy of the receipt and any correspondence.
• Inspect the unit at move‑in and move‑out with the landlord to document condition. | | **Habitability** | • Texas law requires landlords to keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (see Texas Property Code §92.001‑92.004).
• Repairs for major issues (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural) must be made promptly. | • Report problems in writing (email or text) and keep copies.
• If the landlord fails to repair, you may withhold rent (after following the proper procedure) or pursue a repair‑and‑deduct claim. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are **reasonable** (not a penalty). | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if you’re having trouble. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlords must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hrs) before entering, except in emergencies.
• “Reasonable notice” means a notice that is reasonable under the circumstances, not a fixed number of hours. | • Ask for a written notice if you’re unsure.
• Keep a log of entries. | | **Privacy** | • Landlords cannot enter without notice, except in emergencies.
• They cannot interfere with your right to quiet enjoyment. | • If you feel your privacy is violated, document the incident and consider filing a complaint. | | **Discrimination** | • Under the **Fair Housing Act** and Texas law, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • Report discrimination to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a lease with the required notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month).
• Landlords must provide a **written notice** of termination. | • Keep copies of all notices. | | **Eviction Process** | • Texas requires a **notice to quit** (30 days for nonpayment, 7 days for lease violations).
• After the notice period, the landlord must file an eviction action in court. | • Respond to the notice promptly.
• Attend the court hearing; you can present evidence of payment or repair attempts. | | **Repair‑and‑Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but you must follow the proper procedure (written notice, receipts, etc.). | • Keep receipts and document the defect. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has **no statewide rent‑control laws**. | • Your rent can increase only as allowed by the lease or by a new lease agreement. | | **Tenant’s Right to Organize** | • Tenants may form or join a tenant association. | • Use the association to advocate for better conditions or to address landlord misconduct. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Texas offers free or low‑cost legal aid through community legal services, law school clinics, and the Texas Legal Services Center. | • Contact a local legal aid office if you need representation. | ### Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read your lease carefully** – note rent amount, due date, security deposit limits, notice periods, and any repair responsibilities. 2. **Document everything** – photos, videos, written communications, and receipts. 3. **Know your rights** – especially regarding habitability, privacy, and discrimination. 4. **Respond promptly** – to notices, repair requests, and rent payments. 5. **Seek help early** – if you face a dispute, contact a tenant‑rights group or legal aid before the situation escalates. --- #### Useful Resources | Resource | What it Offers | Link | |----------|----------------|------| | Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) | Tenant‑landlord information, complaint filing | https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us/ | | Texas Legal Services Center | Free legal assistance for low‑income Texans | https://www.texaslegalservices.org/ | | HUD Fair Housing Hotline | Report discrimination | https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp | | Texas Tenant Association (if available in your area) | Advocacy, education | Search online for local tenant groups | Feel free to ask if you need more detail on any specific point or if you’d like guidance on how to handle a particular issue (e.g., a landlord refusing to make repairs, a dispute over a security deposit, or a notice of eviction).
